title: A letter
summary: A lad you played with in the under-twelves writes to you from prison. He doesn't ask for anything. He just says he watches you on a telly on the landing. Your mum knew his mum. A season on, he's out.

ends.title: The car wash
ends.text: A lad from your under-twelves wrote to you from prison and you wrote back. He's out, and he washes your car on Saturdays, and won't take money for it.

ends.title: No reply
ends.text: A lad from your under-twelves wrote to you from prison. You didn't write back. Your mum says he's out now and doing all right.

event.title: A letter
event.speaker: mum
setup: A letter, forwarded by the club, from a prison you know the name of. It's from a lad you played with in the under-twelves. Left back. Good left foot.
"I'm not asking for anything. We watch you on the telly on the landing. The lads don't believe I know you. That's all."

say: You ring your mum. {mum.short}: "His mum used to give you lifts. She's had a terrible time with him. He was a lovely lad, at twelve."

replies.label: "I'll send a signed photo. That's all."

write.text: One page. You tell him about the under-twelves cup run, and that his left foot was better than yours. He writes back eleven pages.

photo.text: A signed photo: "To the best left foot I played with." His mum rings yours to say it's on his wall.

no.text: "That's all right, love. You don't have to." She tells his mum you said hello.

beats.title: Out

event.title: Out
event.speaker: mum
setup: A season on. Saturday morning, the car wash by the ring road. The lad holding the hose is twenty-something with a good left foot. He sees your car and stops.

choices.label: Get out and shake his hand.

outcomes.text: He wipes his hand on his trousers before he shakes yours. He won't take money. "Every Saturday," he says. "I'll do it every Saturday." He does.
He shakes it. He doesn't mention the letter. He does the car very carefully and takes the money.

choices.label: Wind the window down and say hello.

outcomes.text: "Eleven pages," he says. "Sorry about that." He won't take your money.
"All right?" "All right." He does the car. You tip him well.

beats.hint: A season on, an old team-mate
